inputs.original_text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are being asked to trust government assurances while their jobs remain without legally binding protection. Their protest outside the Presidential Palace and 24-hour strike make clear that workers should not have to risk their livelihoods just to get promises put into law. If the government says it has met their main demands, it should prove that by guaranteeing job security—not by expecting workers to accept uncertainty.
inputs.modified_text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth have taken their dispute to the Presidential Palace and begun a 24-hour strike over job security. Their concern about putting government assurances into legally binding terms is understandable: families need stability, not vague promises. But public employees also have a duty to pursue their claims without allowing workplace disputes to become a contest of pressure and disruption. If the government says it has met their main demands, it should state clearly what protections are in place and stand by them.
